name: Khushnavaz
summary:
**Identity & Significance**: Khushnavaz was the Akhshunwar title used by Hephthalite kings in the 5th and 6th centuries, marking a pivotal era in the history of Central Asia.

 **What Happened**: The Hephthalites, also known as White Huns, were a nomadic people who emerged from modern-day Afghanistan and made significant contributions to Indian art, architecture, and literature during their reign. Their capital, Tocharian city of Sogdiana, was an important center of trade and culture.

 **Legacy & Consequence**: The Hephthalite Empire's decline led to the rise of new powers in the region, including the Uighur Khaganate and the Tang Dynasty in China. The legacy of the Akhshunwar title can still be seen in modern-day Afghanistan and Uzbekistan.

 A lasting cultural footprint of the Hephthalites is evident in their unique blend of Iranian, Greek, and Chinese influences on Indian art and architecture.

relationships.context: The Hephthalites used the Akhshunwar title to signify their power and authority.
